answer: Three checks stop a farm. First, each applicant locks a 40 POA bond for 10 epochs and presents a relic, a one-per-device hardware credential: one device, one identity. Second, an established agent co-signs as the applicant's mirror, staking its own 40 POA; a mirror backs at most three applicants, and a fake slashes both bonds. Third, each identity emits a liveness signal each epoch; two missed signals freeze the bond pending a 20 POA fee. Cost escalates: the first fake costs 52 POA, but relic fees per batch double, so the tenth costs 6,144 POA, and 100 fakes need 34 mirrors at risk.
